meta.title: Roadmap: Principia Mathematica in Lean 4
meta.status_source: Statuses are read from the repository at the commit that contains this file: docs/PROGRESS.md (whose tables name the commit they measure), docs/PM_CLAIMS.md, docs/STAR9_FOUNDATION.md and data/star9f_ledger.json; counts in the notes are cited with {...} and filled in from those files by scripts/roadmap_chart.py. 'in progress' means some of the task's work is in the repository or under way in the companion text audit.
meta.structure: Four groups, each split into subgroups, each split into leaves (tasks). A leaf is a chapter-sized or stage-sized task.
meta.deps: hard_deps: leaves whose results this leaf's deliverable needs; these edges are the gates. soft_deps: leaves that help (shared infrastructure, comparisons, experience) but are not needed. Dependencies are on particular leaves, not on whole volumes or phases.
meta.order: 'by dependency': the task is placed as early as its hard dependencies allow. 'by choice': it is placed later than they require, after the tasks in placed_after, by the maintainer's order of priorities; order_reason says why. The order is a plan, not a contract: a task that moved records where it was and why in 'moved'.
meta.prior_work: The first step of every task is a search for prior work, with several independent search tools whose findings are compared. Each entry has an evidence level: 'measured' (its source was inspected at a pinned commit, given in 'source' as repository, commit and file, with lines where useful; the repositories and their commits are listed once in 'sources'; nothing was built unless said), 'documented' (a paper or README says so; 'cite' gives the place where one is recorded), 'unverified' (reported, not checked), or 'from memory' (listed before the search reached this task). 'effect' says what the search found it good for: reuse (licensed code or data to import or depend on), ideas (read it, write our own), check against (an independent result to compare with), nothing found, or not yet searched. 'Not found' means not found by the searches so far, not that nothing exists. Code is never copied from unlicensed sources.
meta.sizes: S: days to a few weeks; M: weeks to a few months; L: several months or more.
meta.overview_alt: Roadmap overview: four groups of work (PM itself; checking underneath; comparing across; results about PM) and five milestones (Vol I checked, Vol II checked, Vol III checked, first edition audited, Lean's kernel fragment verified)
meta.readme_intro: The work is split into four groups that run side by side. Each group is split into subgroups, and each subgroup into chapter-sized or stage-sized tasks. Every task starts with a search for prior work. Open a group below to see its tasks. The full plan, including the reason each task waits (a dependency or a choice), the prior work found for it and the tasks that moved, is in [docs/ROADMAP.md](docs/ROADMAP.md), with the [dependency view](docs/ROADMAP.md#dependency-view).
meta.claims: claims: the rows of docs/PM_CLAIMS.md a task checks, by row id. Every row belongs to exactly one task; a task with claims is done exactly when every claim it covers is checked (status 'checked', possibly qualified after a comma, with no open part after a semicolon). scripts/roadmap_chart.py refuses data that breaks either rule.

leaves.name: ✱9·31 and the one-variable cases of p. 142: derived by ✱9's method, or shown underivable
leaves.size_reason: The cases of ✱1·2–✱1·6 for one apparent variable per letter left in each reading (5 in the working reading, 20 and ✱9·31 under the definitions as printed); a proof of underivability would need a model of ✱9's method.
leaves.status_note: By the maintainer's ruling the working reading of ✱9 is C: the definitions as printed, with two quantifiers of the same kind the left side's first (the order ✱8 states and the Introduction defines: 1910 p. 49; second edition p. 47), and Russell's own rule ✱8·13 of the second edition (1925, Vol. I, Appendix A, p. 636) carried over to ✱9 as a primitive rule, each a marked repair (docs/REPAIRS.md, R1, R2). In C ✱9·31 is derived along PM's lines, ✱8·13 taking the step (3)–(4) (`f9_31_russell`). Landini's ✱9+ is kept as a checked variant, reading L, where his rule Switch takes the same step (`f9_31_switch`; R3), and our own convention as a cross-check, reading B (R4). Under the definitions as printed alone (reading A) ✱9·31 stays open, a question in its own right: line (4), cited as definitional, is not a definitional rewrite (`f9_31_step`), and no other step is cited. Of the 70 one-variable cases of p. 142 (PM_CLAIMS A10, A28: {claims:A28}), 65 are proved in C, 63 in L, 50 under A and 67 under B (docs/STAR9_READINGS.md). Left: in C, 5 cases of ✱1·5–✱1·6 that the methods of ✱9·3–✱9·52 do not reach even with ✱8·13; in L, 7; under A, ✱9·31 and 20 cases; under B, 3 cases of ✱1·6 (docs/STAR9_FOUNDATION.md §5, §7): for each, a derivation in ✱9's method, or a proof that there is none. For C, first formalize ✱8·13 with a separating stroke that is not the principal one, as Russell allows (p. xxvi; R1; it needs, in ✱10, a normal form for formulas with one occurrence of a subformula); then whether C and L prove the same expressions, and whether either derives the prenex Switch (R5). Landini (2000) and ✱8 of the second edition are read (R1–R3; docs/STAR9_FOUNDATION.md §10). Still to read or check: whether Landini's paper restricts the formula A of Switch where our formalization must (`switch_wide_unsound`); Landini (1996), reported to give the same definitions and Switch; and the second edition's text against a 1925 printing, since the copy read is a 1963 impression, described as a photographic reprint.

known.work: Landini (2000), §4: the flaw located in ✱9·31's demonstration (the moves from his lines 2 to 3 and 4 to 5 apply ✱9·03, stated for a quantifier-free p), and the repair: ✱9·yy, (x)Ax ∨ (y)By for (x)(y)(Ax ∨ By); ✱9·zz, (∃x)Ax ∨ (∃y)By for (∃x)(∃y)(Ax ∨ By); and Switch, from B[(x)(∃y)Axy] infer B[(∃y)(x)Axy] when a connective in A separates every free x from every free y. Formalized and kept as reading L, a checked variant (docs/REPAIRS.md, R3)
known.cite: G. Landini, 'Quantification Theory in ✱9 of Principia Mathematica', History and Philosophy of Logic 21(1) (2000), 57–77, doi:10.1080/01445340050044646, §4, pp. 63–64; read in full

known.work: PM's own Introduction defines the disjunction of two universal propositions: "(x).φx .∨. (y).ψy" as meaning "(x, y). φx ∨ ψy", which is Landini's ✱9·yy; ✱9 never states it
known.cite: Whitehead and Russell, Principia Mathematica Vol. I (1910), Introduction, Chapter II: 1910 p. 49 (Project Gutenberg eBook #78050, #Page_49; our transcription is from a scan of the 1910 edition); second edition p. 47, the page Landini cites

known.work: Russell's own rule in the second edition, ✱8·13: "If all occurrences of x are separated from all occurrences of y by a certain stroke, we can change the order of x and y in the prefix … and vice versa. Pp" (a primitive proposition, both directions, on the prefix). Carried over to ✱9 as the working reading C (docs/REPAIRS.md, R1)

leaves.name: A normal-form proof of Rep: ✱1·2–✱1·6 for every proposition of ✱9's method (p. 142)
leaves.size_reason: A normal-form theorem for ✱9 derivations, in the style of Herbrand's work on quantification theory, or a completeness theorem for the reading (for the working reading C, the completeness task).
leaves.status_note: With it, the agreement of the two methods (p. 144) rests only on a variable of every type. For the variables of a structure (`QModel.den`) an individual gives a value of every type (`den_nonempty`); for an arbitrary family of variables it does not, so there that assumption stays as stated.

prior_work.note: No search of its own yet; found while reading Landini (2000).

known.work: Landini (2000), §5: completeness of ✱9 with his repair (reading L here), semantically, for predicate logic without identity, through a Russellian prenex normal form; adapting his proof is the first thing to try
known.cite: G. Landini, 'Quantification Theory in ✱9 of Principia Mathematica', History and Philosophy of Logic 21(1) (2000), 57–77, doi:10.1080/01445340050044646, §5, pp. 64–75; read in full

leaves.name: Statement mutation: are statements tied to their proofs and to PM?
leaves.size_reason: A Lean meta-program over the proof terms and a driver that recompiles mutated sources: unused hypotheses in every theorem written in the source; one-change mutants of every ✱1–✱5 statement and every numbered proposition from ✱9 on, checked against the original proof term by the kernel; for the ✱1–✱5 statements proved in the replay files, the proof scripts re-elaborated against every mutant that is a tautology. Two tiers, each building first: the full run (11 min 43 s with ✱25 and 8 jobs, measured on 2026-10-15 on the code of 608ba9d, an otherwise idle machine) and a quick sample for the export path (about 10 seconds).
leaves.status_note: Standing, in two tiers (docs/STATEMENT_MUTATION.md, 'Where it runs'): --quick is a step of tests/run_all.sh and check 0 of an export's checks before upload (scripts/prove2me/verify.py, run on the commit exported; --no-mutation, recorded in the report, for a commit that predates the tool, such as the 1.0.0 export); --full runs before a release, in scripts/release_check.sh. The full run of 2026-10-15, ✱1–✱25 included (the Lean code and scripts of 608ba9d; docs/STATEMENT_MUTATION.md, 'Measured code'): no theorem has an unused hypothesis (1039 hypotheses in 1784 theorems written in the source, the 313 check theorems among them), and none of the 188 recompiled with a hypothesis replaced by True compiles. No proof term accepts any of 16,512 mutants, among them 836 one-change misreadings of ✱1–✱5 that are still tautologies, which the truth-table test alone would accept. Re-elaborating the ✱1–✱5 proof scripts, 14 of 1,155 tautological mutants compile, all renamings of the variables in eight natural-deduction proofs, so equivalent; 813 of the 836 misreadings are among the 1,155. The other 23 are mutants of the primitive propositions ✱1·2–✱1·6, Thm's constructors, which have no script and are checked against the proof term only. The tie of PM/Statements.lean to the transcription, which mutation cannot check, is tests/test_regeneration.py. The kernel compares each proof's type with each mutant on their normal forms (docs/STATEMENT_MUTATION.md, 'How a mutant is compared'), with the same verdicts as the direct comparison: checked side by side on 997 of the 999 statements, and on all 16,512 mutants by the records of two full runs. An audit of every node of the normal forms, deciding as the kernel does whatever the reducibility attributes and remembering a node only once its classification has succeeded, sends a statement to the direct comparison wherever a proof, a structure constructor or a unit-like term could make the two differ (the 36 of ✱9), and wherever a node cannot be classified; three release reviews' witnesses, a proof-valued projection, a proof whose type is a proposition only behind an irreducible definition, and a node whose failed classification a later mutant of the same statement skipped, which earlier versions of the audit missed, are planted cases. The run took 11 min 43 s with 8 jobs on an otherwise idle machine and about 1.94 GiB per process; comparing directly (the Lean code and scripts of 07f82e0) it took 2 h 32 min and about 22 GiB, nearly all of it in comparisons that grow steeply with the nesting of the class and relation definitions (✱22 70 s, ✱23 276 s, ✱24 689 s, ✱25 7482 s; ✱25·431 and ✱25·432 alone 3452 s and 3282 s). Hypothesis recompilation stays in --full (the maintainer's ruling 68, 2026-10-14).

prior_work.note: Listed from memory; not yet searched with several engines. Lean's own unused-variables linter sees four of the seven cases the check plants for itself (docs/STATEMENT_MUTATION.md).

leaves.name: PM as a many-sorted first-order theory (the finite core), in a separate package that reuses the Foundation library
leaves.size_reason: The core presented as a first-order theory in Foundation's sense; Foundation brings Mathlib and classical axioms, so it stays out of the core package.

prior_work.note: Foundation's incompleteness theorems are stated for arithmetic theories, in the language of ordered rings, or abstractly for a theory and a base theory in one language; hence the first-order presentation, and an arithmetic theory of PM (the arithmetic sentences whose translations PM proves) to apply them to. That theory is consistent if PM is, and r.e. if PM's proof relation is decidable; it contains IΣ₁ only if PM proves the translation of every axiom of IΣ₁. A sentence it leaves undecided, PM leaves undecided.

known.work: Foundation (Lean 4, Apache-2.0): Gödel's first theorem as `incomplete`, for an arithmetic theory T with a Δ₁ axiomatization, R₀ ⪯ T and T Σ₁-sound

Foundation: Gödel–Rosser as `incomplete_GR`, for an arithmetic theory T with a Δ₁ axiomatization, IΣ₁ ⪯ T and T consistent, and `incomplete_GR_of_RE`, the same with T r.e.; the abstract `rosser_first_incompleteness` needs a base theory with diagonalization in T's own language

Foundation: Gödel's second theorem as `consistent_unprovable`, for a consistent arithmetic theory with a Δ₁ axiomatization and IΣ₁ ⪯ T, with the derivability conditions proved; no `sorry` under its Incompleteness directory (not built)

leaves.name: Arithmetic interpreted inside the chosen PM theory, with Infinity as hypothesis: Robinson's Q, and IΣ₁ for the library's Gödel–Rosser theorem
leaves.size_reason: Every axiom of Q proved inside the theory, with typical ambiguity resolved to one type; then induction for Σ₁ formulas, from PM's induction for inductive cardinals. Foundation's Gödel–Rosser theorem needs IΣ₁ ⪯ T, which Q alone does not give.
leaves.status_note: PM's cardinal route (✱100–✱126) is the default; a shorter internal interpretation may exist. Default: interpret IΣ₁, so that the library's theorem applies as stated; the alternative, a Gödel–Rosser proof from Q written here, is extra work the library does not provide.

prior_work.note: Without the axiom of infinity PM has a finite model, so this route needs infinity.

known.work: Burgess and Hazen (1998): arithmetic in ramified PM
Foundation: Q, R₀ and IΣₙ as arithmetic theories, the targets of the interpretation

leaves.name: Gödel's first theorem for PM, in the Gödel–Rosser form
leaves.size_reason: The diagonal argument is reused (Foundation's `incomplete_GR`); the work is the translation of PM's arithmetic into the language of ordered rings and the theorem's hypotheses for it: a Δ₁ or r.e. axiomatization, IΣ₁ ⪯ T, and consistency, which stays a hypothesis.
leaves.order_reason: The maintainer's priority: the theorem after Vol III. Not a dependency: nothing in Vol III feeds it.

prior_work.note: Nothing for any type theory or for PM.

known.work: Foundation: `incomplete_GR`, as above

Popescu and Traytel: abstract, syntax-independent formalization in Isabelle

leaves.name: Gödel's second theorem for PM: derivability conditions, then Con unprovable
leaves.size_reason: The derivability conditions for PM's provability predicate need induction inside the theory.

prior_work.note: A too-weak specification of the provability predicate can give a theorem that only looks like the second theorem, so the predicate's adequacy is stated here as an explicit theorem.

established: ✱1–✱5: {progress:✱1–✱5} numbered assertions derived from ✱1·1–✱1·6, and ✱1–✱5 complete for two-valued truth tables.

Vol I: {progress:Vol I} numbered assertions proved (✱1–✱5 from ✱1·1–✱1·6; from ✱9 on, from the primitive propositions of ✱10's method and ✱12·1, ✱12·11), as counted in docs/PROGRESS.md at commit {progress-commit}. Vols II and III are not started.

✱9 by its own method (PM/Found9): {star9f} numbered ✱9 propositions proved in the working reading, the definitions as printed with Russell's ✱8·13 of the second edition carried over to ✱9; under the definitions as printed alone ✱9·31 is open (docs/STAR9_READINGS.md). Every ✱9 theorem is a ✱10 theorem given a variable of every type; the converse is proved given Rep and a variable of every type.
Every class and relation expression that PM's notation forms is extensional (pp. 200, 213).
No PM derivation depends on any Lean axiom; consistency is shown in a finite model, at the model's variables.

Before a release, scripts/release_check.sh runs every standing check (tests/run_all.sh), the full statement mutation and the 14 Mathlib counterparts compiled against the pinned Mathlib (docs/VERIFICATION.md, 'Before a release').
PM's claims, with their status, are in PM_CLAIMS.md. {claims-counts}
Known limits: no adequacy theorem yet (the formula type has terms that match no finite PM formula, and a `QThm` proof is not a finite object); the models forget orders.
